S01.kontekst: The institution's legal department participates in an international technical assistance project. The partner has offered the institution ten places on a four-day training programme in London; two are allocated to the legal department. Equal access to development, relevance to the programme, integrity in professional contacts and practical use of the learning must be balanced.

diiovi_osoby.opys: Selects two legal department representatives and is responsible for the criteria and practical results of the trip.
Has the most legal experience, specialising in litigation. Knows the law but can be condescending. Has attended similar events before.
Less experienced, responsible and approachable, with colleagues' trust. Has worked on the institution's anti-corruption documents.
Recently joined the department, has a good command of English and is interested in international law. She has limited practical experience so far.
Discusses the delegation, staff development and how training meets the institution's needs.
Approves official decisions and expects an account of the resources spent.

S01.sytuatsiia: The institution has ten places on a four-day training programme in London. You must select two legal department representatives. The programme is not yet final. Participation offers opportunities for development, international contacts and career progression. There are three candidates: an experienced litigation lawyer, a dependable internal procedures specialist and a young international law specialist with good English but little practical experience.

tsinnosti_v_konflikti.poiasnennia: Transparent criteria take time; a quick appointment without explanation can weaken trust.
Language skills and potential must be weighed against experience and the specific programme.
An informal meeting may be useful, but private interests and gift rules must be checked.

vuzly.tekst:
Stage 1 · Allocating two places

The institution has ten places on a four-day training programme in London. You must select two legal department representatives. The programme is not yet final. Participation offers opportunities for development, international contacts and career progression. There are three candidates: an experienced litigation lawyer, a dependable internal procedures specialist and a young international law specialist with good English but little practical experience.
vuzly.zapytannia: Whom will you select for the training trip?

varianty.tekst: The experienced lawyer and the internal procedures specialist — prioritise experience.

naslidky.odrazu: Two experienced colleagues receive places. The international law specialist may lose motivation; the team does not understand the criteria.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Giving seniority an entrenched advantage unrelated to training objectives may limit younger staff's development and weaken trust in selection.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (0): without criteria, neither bias nor equal selection can be confirmed. Effectiveness (+1): experience allows a delegation to be formed quickly, but programme relevance has not been checked. Trust (−1): the colleague not selected cannot see clear reasons.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Seniority as a guide, with a risk of opacity. Experience is useful, but it is not yet clear whether these particular competencies match the programme. A single refusal of training does not in itself establish mobbing. Systematic, unjustified restrictions require assessment under Articles 2-1 and 2-2 of the Labour Code; mobbing requires the statutory elements to be established, rather than mere disagreement with the selection.

varianty.tekst: The experienced lawyer and the international law specialist — combine experience with development potential.

naslidky.odrazu: The delegation combines experience and language skills, but another candidate questions the reasons for the decision.
naslidky.vidkladeni: If opaque selection recurs, staff may see opportunities as the supervisor's personal choice; objectivity will be hard to demonstrate during a review.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (0): combining skills does not replace consistent criteria. Effectiveness (+1): legal experience is complemented by language skills. Trust (0): development is supported, but the reasons for excluding another colleague remain unexplained.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: A management balance without a sufficient procedure. Combining experience and language skills may be useful. However, the internal procedures specialist is entitled to a clear explanation of why his expertise was less relevant.

varianty.tekst: The internal procedures specialist and the international law specialist — give less experienced colleagues an opportunity.

naslidky.odrazu: The two less experienced colleagues are motivated. The experienced lawyer and the head ask why his expertise has not been used.
naslidky.vidkladeni: If development needs become the sole criterion, experienced staff may lose trust and the institution's representation abroad may suffer.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (0): supporting development does not establish equal assessment. Effectiveness (0): new potential is balanced against the risk of undervaluing experience. Trust (+1): access to opportunities is broadened, although the excluded colleague needs an explanation.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Developing the team at the risk of losing relevant experience. Training needs matter but must not automatically outweigh programme relevance and the ability to represent the institution. There is no basis to declare this choice unlawful without examining the criteria and applicable provisions.

varianty.tekst: Do not nominate candidates immediately: hold an open selection using criteria announced in advance.

naslidky.odrazu: Candidates receive equal conditions, while preparing the assessment takes time. Results can be explained.
naslidky.vidkladeni: A repeatable process becomes available for future international projects; trust grows if rules are applied consistently.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+2): criteria are announced before results and apply equally to everyone. Effectiveness (−1): selection takes preparation and time. Trust (+2): each candidate can examine the reasons for the decision.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: A transparent procedure that takes time. Define professional competence, relevance to the programme, language proficiency and ability to apply the results. Consistent criteria and documented results reduce personal preferences, but the assessments themselves must still be checked against the purpose.

vuzly.tekst:
Stage 2 · Selection based on experience

After you select the experienced lawyer and the internal procedures specialist, the deputy head invites you to talk: "The experienced lawyer has attended similar events several times. Perhaps we should give the international law specialist this opportunity? She speaks English and has potential." The supervisor's suggestion alone is not an objective criterion.
vuzly.zapytannia: How will you respond, and whom will you select for the training trip?

varianty.tekst: Keep the delegation unchanged until there are objective grounds to review the results.

naslidky.odrazu: Preparations continue without delay; questions about access to training remain.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Following substantiated rules supports trust, but defending an opaque decision reinforces doubts.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+0): intent alone does not resolve legality. Effectiveness (+1): there is a quick organisational result, although it does not remove all risks. Preparations continue without delay; questions about access to training remain. Trust (-1): Following substantiated rules supports trust, but defending an opaque decision reinforces doubts.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Consistency with a qualification. Stability is justified only if the original selection was properly substantiated. Referring to a decision already made does not remedy the lack of criteria.

varianty.tekst: Nominate the experienced lawyer and the international law specialist, explaining how their skills match the programme.

naslidky.odrazu: Language skills complement experience, but the excluded candidate may challenge the change.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Documented programme relevance may be useful; unexplained rotation will look like personal influence.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+0): intent alone does not resolve legality. Effectiveness (+1): there is a quick organisational result, although it does not remove all risks. Language skills complement experience, but the excluded candidate may challenge the change. Trust (+0): Documented programme relevance may be useful; unexplained rotation will look like personal influence.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: A review needs common grounds. Competence and development potential can complement each other. Do not replace a candidate solely because of the deputy's wishes; assess all candidates under the same rules.

varianty.tekst: Replace the experienced lawyer with the international law specialist: select her and the internal procedures specialist because the experienced colleague has already had similar opportunities.

naslidky.odrazu: Less experienced colleagues gain greater access to international training. The excluded lawyer may demand an explanation; the delegation and documents will need changing.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Transparent rotation rules make development more accessible. Without such rules, repeated replacements look like ad hoc interference and may undermine trust in HR decisions.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (0): rotation may be justified, but common criteria are not yet confirmed. Effectiveness (−1): the delegation and arrangements need changing while the programme remains incomplete. Trust (+1): access to development is broadened; the experienced colleague needs an explanation for the replacement.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Rotating opportunities with a risk of substituting criteria. Previous training participation may be considered under announced staff development rules. However, a younger colleague's development needs or the deputy's wishes do not replace checking all candidates' skills and programme relevance.

varianty.tekst: Reassess all three using the same practical task related to the programme.

naslidky.odrazu: Additional time and an explanation for repeating selection are needed.
naslidky.vidkladeni: A common practical assessment links the decision to training objectives and can restore trust.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+2): the decision rests on fact-checking and a lawful procedure. Effectiveness (-1): further checks or review take time and resources. Additional time and an explanation for repeating selection are needed. Trust (+1): A common practical assessment links the decision to training objectives and can restore trust.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Clarifying the procedure. Define the task, criteria and deadlines in advance. Assessment changes are justified by specific shortcomings or new information rather than a preferred name on the list.

vuzly.tekst:
Stage 2 · Experience and development prospects

After the experienced lawyer and international law specialist are selected, the internal procedures specialist asks for the criteria to be explained. It emerges that he developed internal anti-corruption documents and part of the programme covers this very topic. The selected candidates are motivated, but the absence of clear criteria creates a risk of conflict.
vuzly.zapytannia: How will you respond, and whom will you select for the training trip?

varianty.tekst: Reconsider the internal procedures specialist in light of his anti-corruption experience.

naslidky.odrazu: There is an opportunity to align the delegation more closely with the programme; colleagues already selected may object to changing the selection.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The decision is better substantiated if everyone is checked equally, but without explanations it will seem ad hoc.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+1): one safeguard is supported, but further action is needed. Effectiveness (+0): the immediate result is limited and depends on further action. The delegation can be aligned more closely with the programme; colleagues already selected may object. Trust (+1): The decision is better substantiated if everyone is checked equally, but without explanations it will seem ad hoc.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Relevant new facts. Consider anti-corruption experience alongside the other criteria for all three candidates. Discovering a new competence does not create an automatic entitlement to a place.

varianty.tekst: Keep the delegation unchanged to avoid revising a decision already made.

naslidky.odrazu: Organisational documents need no revision, but the excluded candidate's question remains unanswered.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Ignoring specialisation may reduce the value of training and reinforce perceptions of subjective selection.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+0): intent alone does not resolve legality. Effectiveness (+1): there is a quick organisational result, although it does not remove all risks. Organisational documents need no revision, but the excluded candidate's question remains unanswered. Trust (-1): Ignoring specialisation may reduce the value of training and reinforce perceptions of subjective selection.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Stability does not replace checking. Avoiding inconsistency makes sense if relevant skills have already been considered. Material new information should not be ignored merely to keep the list unchanged.

varianty.tekst: Select the internal procedures specialist and the international law specialist — combine anti-corruption experience and international training while offering them development opportunities.

naslidky.odrazu: The delegation gains practical anti-corruption experience and language skills. The experienced lawyer loses his place and may challenge the review.
naslidky.vidkladeni: If both skills are genuinely needed by the programme, learning outcomes will be easier to apply. Without consistent criteria, the decision will remain difficult to justify to the team or reviewers.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+1): new professional information is considered, but a common procedure still needs confirmation. Effectiveness (0): relevant skills are balanced against organisational revision and programme uncertainty. Trust (0): two colleagues' development is supported, but the reasons for replacing the third still need explanation.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: A balance of skills needs checking. New information about work on anti-corruption documents may change the assessment of a candidate. However, replacing the experienced lawyer simply to support less experienced colleagues leaves the same subjectivity risk. Explain the weight of each criterion for all three.

varianty.tekst: Reassess all three with the same practical task on the training topic.

naslidky.odrazu: Selection takes additional time; everyone can demonstrate practical relevance.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Documented results make the decision easier to explain and reduce the risk of unjustified preferences.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+2): the decision rests on fact-checking and a lawful procedure. Effectiveness (-1): further checks or review take time and resources. Selection takes additional time; everyone can demonstrate practical relevance. Trust (+2): Documented results make the decision easier to explain and reduce the risk of unjustified preferences.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: A consistent approach to review. Explain which new information calls for assessment, and do not tailor the task to a particular candidate.

vuzly.tekst:
Stage 2 · Developing less experienced colleagues

After the internal procedures specialist and international law specialist are selected, the manager asks why the experienced lawyer was not chosen. Colleagues welcome the development opportunity, but overlooking relevant experience may weaken the institution's representation and senior staff members' trust. Development needs should not automatically outweigh suitability for the tasks.
vuzly.zapytannia: How will you respond, and whom will you select for the training trip?

varianty.tekst: Do not nominate candidates immediately: assess all three against common criteria, including relevance to the programme.

naslidky.odrazu: All candidates return to a common procedure; there is a delay, but clear grounds become available.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Staff development is aligned with institutional needs; documented criteria support trust.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+2): the decision rests on fact-checking and a lawful procedure. Effectiveness (-1): further checks or review take time and resources. All candidates return to a common procedure; there is a delay, but clear grounds become available. Trust (+2): Staff development is aligned with institutional needs; documented criteria support trust.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: A common assessment of competence. Development needs and experience must be evaluated against the purpose of the trip. Announce criteria and the procedure before reassessment and explain why the original decision is being reviewed.

varianty.tekst: Postpone nomination until the programme is clarified, without organising a shared assessment yet.

naslidky.odrazu: You avoid deciding on incomplete information, but the nomination window shrinks.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Without an agreed deadline and subsequent assessment, the training opportunity may be lost and doubts about fairness will remain.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+0): intent alone does not resolve legality. Effectiveness (-1): further checks or review take time and resources. You avoid deciding on incomplete information, but the nomination window shrinks. Trust (-1): Without an agreed deadline and subsequent assessment, the training opportunity may be lost and doubts about fairness will remain.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Waiting without a procedure. Clarifying the programme is necessary, but a pause does not itself establish equal criteria. Set a deadline for receiving information to avoid losing both places or leaving candidates uncertain.

vuzly.tekst:
Stage 2 · Reviewing open selection

After assessment, the experienced lawyer has the highest experience score, the international law specialist leads on English and international relevance, and the internal procedures specialist leads on practical anti-corruption documentation work. However, the experienced lawyer argues that the formal scoring system overlooks his actual merits. How will you act?
vuzly.zapytannia: How will you respond to the experienced lawyer's objections to the assessment results?

varianty.tekst: Approve the assessment results because the criteria were the same for everyone.

naslidky.odrazu: Selection concludes. Candidates receive substantiated results. The experienced lawyer may remain dissatisfied.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Following established rules becomes routine. Trust in transparent procedures grows. Proper documentation reduces the risk of accusations of bias.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+1): one safeguard is supported, but further action is needed. Effectiveness (+1): there is a quick organisational result, although it does not remove all risks. Selection concludes. Candidates receive substantiated results. The experienced lawyer may remain dissatisfied. Trust (+1): Following established rules becomes routine. Trust in transparent procedures grows. Proper documentation reduces the risk of accusations of bias.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Following announced criteria. If criteria were set in advance, applied consistently to all candidates and results are documented, there is no reason to change them merely because one participant is dissatisfied.

varianty.tekst: Review the criteria because practical experience may have been given insufficient weight.

naslidky.odrazu: Results lose their finality. The international law specialist and the internal procedures specialist may question procedural fairness. Another opportunity to interfere with results arises.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Criteria may routinely be changed after results are known. Trust in assessment falls. There is a risk of unjustified preferences for individual staff members.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (-1): the approach leaves a significant procedural risk. Effectiveness (-1): further checks or review take time and resources. Results lose their finality. The international law specialist and the internal procedures specialist may question procedural fairness. Another opportunity to interfere with results arises. Trust (-1): Criteria may routinely be changed after results are known. Trust in assessment falls. There is a risk of unjustified preferences for individual staff members.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: A procedural risk if criteria are changed to favour a particular candidate. Criteria may be reviewed if they do not serve the training purpose or were formulated incorrectly. If criteria change, all candidates must be reassessed under the same rules.

varianty.tekst: Arrange an additional interview with the same questions for all candidates.

naslidky.odrazu: All candidates have an equal opportunity to demonstrate knowledge. Results become more complete. Selection takes additional time.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The institution gains a more comprehensive assessment mechanism. Future selection improves. The risk of undervaluing practical skills decreases.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+1): one safeguard is supported, but further action is needed. Effectiveness (-1): further checks or review take time and resources. All candidates have an equal opportunity to demonstrate knowledge. Results become more complete. Selection takes additional time. Trust (+1): The institution gains a more comprehensive assessment process. Future selections improve. The risk of undervaluing practical skills falls.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: A management compromise. An additional interview can test practical skills inadequately assessed initially. However, questions, assessment criteria and the interview procedure must be defined in advance.

varianty.tekst: Ask the panel to recheck results without personally intervening in assessment.

naslidky.odrazu: An additional check is conducted. The risk of personal influence falls. The final decision may be delayed.
naslidky.vidkladeni: An internal control mechanism develops. Trust in assessment results grows. The institution can identify and remedy procedural shortcomings.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+2): the decision rests on fact-checking and a lawful procedure. Effectiveness (-1): further checks or review take time and resources. An additional check is conducted. The risk of personal influence falls. The final decision may be delayed. Trust (+2): An internal control mechanism develops. Trust in assessment results grows. The institution can identify and remedy procedural shortcomings.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: A substantiated approach where the facts are checked. This supports impartiality and allows assessment errors to be checked. It is particularly important that a panel conducts the review rather than a person directly interested in the results.

vuzly.tekst:
Stage 3 · The trip's subject matter changes the situation

You receive the final training programme. It covers international anti-corruption cooperation; transparency in defence procurement; preventing and managing conflicts of interest; and implementing integrity standards in the security and defence sector. Reviewing the candidates' professional profiles, you realise that the experienced lawyer has the greatest legal experience but mainly specialises in litigation. The internal procedures specialist helped develop internal anti-corruption documents. The international law specialist has training in international law and a good command of English. The deputy manager approaches you again: 'We have almost settled on the delegation. But should we consider who can actually bring the greatest benefit to the institution after returning?' Your decision:
vuzly.zapytannia: What will you decide in light of the final programme?

varianty.tekst: Keep the delegation unchanged. Programme relevance should already have been assessed, and repeated changes undermine trust in the procedure.

naslidky.odrazu: The delegation remains unchanged. Another review of the selection is avoided. New professional needs may remain unaddressed.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Without a genuine check, international training becomes less effective. Matching staff skills to official tasks may become a formality. The institution risks missing expected outcomes.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+0): intent alone does not resolve legality. Effectiveness (+1): there is a quick organisational result, although it does not remove all risks. The delegation remains unchanged. Another review of results is avoided. New professional needs may remain unaddressed. Trust (-1): Without a genuine check, international training becomes less effective. Matching staff skills to official tasks may become a formality. The institution risks missing expected outcomes.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Procedural stability with a risk of formalism. Consistency and stability matter. If programme relevance was properly assessed, there is no reason for repeated changes. Stability must not be used to preserve a clearly ineffective decision.

varianty.tekst: Review the delegation in light of new information about the programme and candidates' competence.

naslidky.odrazu: The delegation is reviewed against programme needs. The institution can send the most relevant specialists. Excluded candidates may object.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Participation in the international event becomes more effective. Knowledge is more likely to be applied. Decisions become focused on institutional needs rather than formal measures alone.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+2): the decision rests on fact-checking and a lawful procedure. Effectiveness (-1): further checks or review take time and resources. The delegation is reviewed against programme needs. The institution can send the most relevant specialists. Excluded candidates may object. Trust (+1): Participation in the international event becomes more effective. Knowledge is more likely to be applied. Decisions become focused on institutional needs rather than formal measures alone.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: A substantiated approach where the facts are checked. The new information directly concerns the training purpose. The current delegation must therefore be checked against institutional needs.

varianty.tekst: Assign different tasks: one participant represents the institution and the other handles analytical work.

naslidky.odrazu: Participants receive clear tasks. Duplication falls. The delegation becomes better organised.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Learning outcomes can be used more effectively. Shared allocation of responsibilities becomes routine. International projects deliver better results.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+1): one safeguard is supported, but further action is needed. Effectiveness (+2): clear task allocation reduces duplication and puts expertise to use. Participants receive clear tasks. Duplication falls. The delegation becomes better organised. Trust (+1): Learning outcomes can be used more effectively. Shared allocation of responsibilities becomes routine. International projects deliver better results.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: A management compromise. This is a useful approach because it makes the most of each participant's strengths. However, it must not replace objective selection. First determine who should participate, then allocate tasks.

varianty.tekst: Ask management to approve the final delegation with written reasons for each candidate.

naslidky.odrazu: Management receives reasons for each candidacy. Participants understand the decision better. Misunderstandings become less likely.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Documenting management decisions becomes routine. Spending justification is easier to review. Responsible officials become more accountable.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+1): one safeguard is supported, but further action is needed. Effectiveness (+0): the immediate result is limited and depends on further action. Management receives reasons for each candidacy. Participants understand the decision better. Misunderstandings become less likely. Trust (+2): Documenting management decisions becomes routine. Spending justification is easier to review. Responsible officials become more accountable.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: A management compromise. Documenting reasons improves transparency and helps show that institutional needs informed the delegation. However, written reasons do not replace sound assessment. A document alone does not remedy a biased selection.

vuzly.tekst:
Stage 4 · An unexpected proposal

Two days before departure, the experienced lawyer tells you that a representative of the host organisation is a longstanding professional acquaintance. He proposes an informal meeting to discuss matters outside the official programme. Meanwhile, the internal procedures specialist says he has heard that participants might receive additional gifts from the hosts. What will you do?
vuzly.zapytannia: What will you do about the extra meeting and possible gifts?

varianty.tekst: Allow an informal meeting if it fits the programme and supports professional contacts.

naslidky.odrazu: Participants can make additional professional contacts. The meeting may benefit international cooperation. Without prior checking, its purpose may be misunderstood. Gifts and extra advantages may raise questions.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Informal contacts may develop into mutual expectations about future decisions. A private interest may create an actual or potential conflict of interest. The impartiality of institutional representatives may be questioned.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+0): intent alone does not resolve legality. Effectiveness (+1): there is a quick organisational result, although it does not remove all risks. Participants can make additional professional contacts. The meeting may benefit international cooperation. Without prior checking, its purpose may be misunderstood. Gifts and extra advantages may raise questions. Trust (-1): Informal contacts may develop into mutual expectations about future decisions. A private interest may create an actual or potential conflict of interest. The impartiality of institutional representatives may be questioned.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Professional contacts require risk checks. Such contacts and informal communication are not themselves prohibited. However, the experienced lawyer's acquaintance at the host organisation and possible extra gifts require examination. An acquaintance alone does not establish a conflict of interest, but a private interest connected with official powers requires appropriate conflict-management measures.

varianty.tekst: Require all extra meetings to be reported in advance and approved through official procedures.

naslidky.odrazu: Uncontrolled contacts become less likely. The institution learns about extra meetings. Participants understand acceptable conduct. International engagement becomes more transparent.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Supervised professional contacts become routine. Using official position for personal advantages becomes less likely. International partners' trust in the institution grows.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+2): the decision rests on fact-checking and a lawful procedure. Effectiveness (-1): further checks or review take time and resources. Uncontrolled contacts become less likely. The institution learns about extra meetings. Participants understand acceptable conduct. International engagement becomes more transparent. Trust (+2): Supervised professional contacts become routine. Using official position for personal advantages becomes less likely. International partners' trust in the institution grows.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: A substantiated approach where the facts are checked. This permits oversight of official contacts and checking their purpose beforehand. Prior approval helps establish attendees, the official purpose, possible conflicts of interest, compliance with gift rules and whether other institutional representatives should attend. Approval is not blanket permission: even an officially approved meeting does not legalise an undue benefit or a breach of gift restrictions.

varianty.tekst: Prohibit all informal contacts to avoid even potential reputational risks.

naslidky.odrazu: Participants avoid extra meetings. The risk of improper advantages during informal communication falls. Potentially useful professional contacts are also lost.
naslidky.vidkladeni: International cooperation may become excessively formal. The institution loses professional exchange opportunities. Staff may see anti-corruption restrictions as obstacles to normal official work.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+0): intent alone does not resolve legality. Effectiveness (-1): further checks or review take time and resources. Participants avoid extra meetings. The risk of improper advantages during informal communication falls. Potentially useful professional contacts are also lost. Trust (-1): International cooperation may become excessively formal. The institution loses professional exchange opportunities. Staff may see anti-corruption restrictions as obstacles to normal official work.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: An excessive restriction. This attempts to avoid corruption risks through an overly restrictive approach. The law does not ban all informal professional contacts. International cooperation often involves working meetings, exchanges of experience and professional discussion outside the main programme. A balanced approach defines permissible conditions rather than banning all contacts.

varianty.tekst: Allow the meeting but require participants to record its results and report offers or gifts in writing.

naslidky.odrazu: Participants may gain professional contacts. The institution receives documented results. An improper offer may be discovered only after acceptance.
naslidky.vidkladeni: With proper oversight, transparent reporting develops. Without prior oversight, reputational and legal consequences remain possible. Documentation helps check compliance but does not undo an offence already committed.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+1): one safeguard is supported, but further action is needed. Effectiveness (+1): there is a quick organisational result, although it does not remove all risks. Participants may gain professional contacts. The institution receives documented results. An improper offer may be discovered only after acceptance. Trust (+0): With proper oversight, transparent reporting develops. Without prior oversight, reputational and legal consequences remain possible. Documentation helps check compliance but does not undo an offence already committed.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Documentation without prior oversight. This records meeting outcomes and offers. Participants do not conceal additional professional contacts, and the institution learns about them. However, a post-meeting report does not replace prior risk checks. Reporting a gift also does not mean it may be accepted.

vuzly.tekst:
Stage 5 · Returning and taking responsibility for results

The two selected representatives have returned. They involve departmental colleagues in processing the materials; the third candidate receives no additional place. The institution's manager expects a report and specific proposals for applying the learning. However, the participants and colleagues involved assess the results differently. The experienced lawyer considers professional contacts the most valuable outcome. The internal procedures specialist has prepared proposals to improve anti-corruption procedures. The international law specialist wants to train other staff but lacks sufficient practical experience. The manager says: 'We spent public funds. I want to see a real result, not just a trip report.' What will you decide?
vuzly.zapytannia: How will you secure practical learning outcomes?

varianty.tekst: Have all participants prepare a joint report on the training results.

naslidky.odrazu: The institution receives an overview of the trip's outcomes. Participants organise what they learned. Management can assess the value of training.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Without follow-up, the report may remain a formality. Knowledge may not be applied. Training expenditure may fail to deliver expected results.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+1): one safeguard is supported, but further action is needed. Effectiveness (+0): the immediate result is limited and depends on further action. The institution receives an overview of the trip's outcomes. Participants organise what they learned. Management can assess the value of training. Trust (+1): Without follow-up, the report may remain a formality. Knowledge may not be applied. Training expenditure may fail to deliver expected results.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Reporting requires follow-up. A joint report summarises knowledge, records key outcomes and identifies potential uses. It must not be a mere formality: it should contain specific proposals and explain how the knowledge can be used in the institution's work.

varianty.tekst: Give each participant a separate task matched to their expertise.

naslidky.odrazu: Each participant has individual responsibility. Work is allocated by expertise. Task duplication becomes less likely.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The institution receives concrete analytical and practical materials. Individual accountability increases. Applying professional learning becomes routine.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Integrity (+1): one safeguard is supported, but further action is needed. Effectiveness (+1): there is a quick organisational result, although it does not remove all risks.
